newsitem.title: USA: Triton Q3 enhanced by Colombian production.
newsitem.headline: Triton Q3 enhanced by Colombian production.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd said Tuesday the third quarter was its most profitable quarter in three years, with results enhanced by steady production from Colombia's Cusiana field.
The company reported earnings after preferred dividends for the latest quarter of $18.6 million, or $0.50 per share, compared with $900,000, or $0.03 per share, for the year earler quarter.
The third quarter of 1996 was the most profitable quarter for the company since the third quarter of 1993, when Triton sold its Canadian subsidiary, it noted.
Triton and its partners achieved production from the Cusiana and Cupiagua fields that averaged some 172,000 barrels of oil per day during the quarter, the company said.
Triton has a 12 percent interest in these fields. Its partners are British Petroleum Co Plc, Total SA and Colombia's national oil company.

During the latest quarter, Triton said, it purchased an additional $20 million of its senior subordinated discount notes due 1997 at a price below face value. The aggregate face value of the remaining 1997 Notes amounts to $210 million.
Third-quarter 1996 earnings included $10.1 million of nonrecurring items, including an $8.7 million after-tax gain from the sale of Triton's Crusader Ltd holdings.
For the first nine months of 1996, earnings after preferred dividends were $41.4 million, or $1.12 per share, up from $1.3 million, or $0.04 per share, a year earlier.

Year-to-date 1996 results were helped by a low effective tax rate. Triton said it recognized a portion of the expected benefit associated with current and future utilization of net operating loss carryforwards that partially offset tax expense in the United States and Colombia.
